name: Jacques Demy
milestone_by_age_26: Won an Honorable Mention at the 1956 Berlin International Film Festival for his short documentary film 'Le Sabotier du Val de Loire' (1955), at age 24-25.
early_history_summary: Demy grew up in Pontchâteau and Nantes in a working-class family; his father owned a garage and his mother was a hairdresser, but both were passionate about cinema and popular opera. He created a puppet theatre at age 4, made his first animated film at 9 by hand-painting film strips, and bought his first film camera at 13. He became a cinéphile and attended a ciné-club in Nantes by 14. Director Christian-Jaque was impressed by the young filmmaker and sponsored his entry into the ETPC film school in Paris. After graduating in 1952, he worked as assistant to animator Paul Grimault and documentarist Georges Rouquier before making his first notable short film in 1955.

evidence_summary: Demy was immersed in cinema culture from an exceptionally young age, making animated films at 9 and owning a camera by 13, encouraged by cinema-loving parents in working-class France. Director Christian-Jaque sponsored his entry into the ETPC film school in Paris, and he apprenticed under animator Paul Grimault and documentarist Georges Rouquier.
